pool_config.pool_brief: Build an asynchronous system using Promises and async/await. Your solution must use: a custom function that returns a new Promise (with resolve and reject), async/await to consume promises, try/catch for error handling, Promise.all for parallel operations, a comparison of sequential vs parallel execution (using console.time), and at least one retry pattern. All variables must use const or let.

projects.title: Carbon Loan Processing Pipeline
projects.scenario: Build an async loan processing system for Carbon. Simulate API calls with Promises, process loan applications sequentially and in parallel, handle failures with retry logic, and compare execution times.
requirements: Create a function `simulateAPI(data, delay, shouldFail)` that returns a new Promise — resolves with data after delay, or rejects with an Error if shouldFail is true
Write an async function `processLoan(applicant)` that awaits 3 sequential steps: creditCheck → verifyIncome → approveLoan (each using simulateAPI with ~500ms delay); log each step
Add try/catch error handling: if any step fails, log the error message and return a rejection reason
Write an async function `processBatch(applicants)` that uses Promise.all to process multiple applicants in parallel; log all results
Compare sequential vs parallel: process 3 applicants sequentially (one after another with await in a loop) then in parallel (Promise.all); use console.time/timeEnd to show the speed difference
Implement a retry function `withRetry(fn, retries)` that retries a failing async function up to N times before giving up; demonstrate it with a function that fails twice then succeeds

projects.title: Termii OTP Delivery System
projects.scenario: Build an async OTP delivery system for Termii. Simulate sending OTPs via multiple channels, handle delivery failures with retries, and process bulk sends in parallel.
requirements: Create a function `sendOTP(channel, phone, delay)` that returns a new Promise — resolves with a success message after delay, or rejects if channel is 'whatsapp' (simulating failure)
Write an async function `deliverOTP(phone)` that awaits 3 sequential steps: generateCode → sendSMS → logDelivery (each using a Promise with ~400ms delay); log each step
Add try/catch: if sending fails, catch the error, log it, and attempt a fallback channel
Write an async function `bulkSend(phones)` that uses Promise.all to send OTPs to multiple numbers in parallel; log results
Compare sequential vs parallel: send to 4 numbers sequentially, then in parallel; use console.time/timeEnd to show the difference
Implement a retry: if the primary channel fails, retry up to 3 times with a different channel before giving up

projects.title: Bamboo Stock Trading Engine
projects.scenario: Build an async stock trading system for Bamboo. Simulate fetching stock prices, executing trades with validation, handling failures, and batch-processing orders in parallel.
requirements: Create a function `fetchPrice(symbol, delay)` that returns a new Promise resolving with a random price after the delay; reject if symbol is 'INVALID'
Write an async function `executeTrade(order)` that awaits 3 sequential steps: fetchPrice → validateFunds → confirmTrade (each ~400ms); log each step with the symbol
Add try/catch: if any step fails (invalid symbol or insufficient funds), log the error and mark the trade as failed
Write an async function `batchTrade(orders)` that uses Promise.all to execute multiple trades in parallel; use Promise.allSettled to handle mixed success/failure
Compare sequential vs parallel: execute 3 trades sequentially, then in parallel; log timing with console.time/timeEnd
Implement retry: if fetchPrice fails due to timeout, retry up to 2 times before marking as failed

projects.title: Korapay Payment Gateway Simulator
projects.scenario: Build an async payment gateway simulator for Korapay. Simulate charge operations, handle declined payments, process merchant settlements in parallel, and implement retry logic.
requirements: Create a function `chargeCard(amount, delay)` that returns a new Promise — resolves with a transaction reference after delay; rejects if amount > 100000 (limit exceeded)
Write an async function `processPayment(payment)` that awaits 3 sequential steps: validateCard → chargeCard → issueReceipt (each ~500ms); log each step
Add try/catch: if the charge is declined, log the reason and return a failed payment object
Write an async function `settleMultiple(payments)` that uses Promise.all to process multiple payments in parallel; log all results together
Compare sequential vs parallel: process 3 payments both ways; log timing with console.time/timeEnd
Implement retry: if chargeCard fails with a temporary error, retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff (delay doubles each retry)

projects.title: Interswitch Transaction Reconciliation
projects.scenario: Build an async transaction reconciliation system for Interswitch. Simulate fetching records from multiple sources, compare them, handle fetch failures, and process reconciliations in parallel.
requirements: Create a function `fetchRecords(source, delay)` that returns a new Promise resolving with mock transaction data after delay; rejects if source is 'offline'
Write an async function `reconcile(txnId)` that awaits 3 sequential steps: fetchBankRecord → fetchMerchantRecord → compareRecords (each ~400ms); log matches/mismatches
Add try/catch: if either source is unavailable, catch the error and log which source failed
Write an async function `batchReconcile(txnIds)` that uses Promise.all to reconcile multiple transactions in parallel
Compare sequential vs parallel: reconcile 4 transactions both ways; log timing with console.time/timeEnd
Implement retry: if a fetch fails, retry up to 2 times before marking as unreconciled

descriptors.full: Custom function returns new Promise with resolve/reject; async functions use await correctly; code is flat and readable (not nested .then() chains)
descriptors.partial: Promise created but resolve/reject not both used, or await used incorrectly
descriptors.none: No Promise creation; no async/await usage

descriptors.full: try/catch wraps await calls correctly; error messages are logged clearly; rejected promises are handled without unhandled rejection warnings; retry pattern implemented
descriptors.partial: try/catch present but doesn't cover all failure cases, or retry missing
descriptors.none: No error handling; unhandled rejections likely

descriptors.full: Promise.all used correctly for parallel execution; sequential and parallel approaches both demonstrated; console.time/timeEnd proves the speed difference; results are correct
descriptors.partial: Promise.all used but timing comparison missing, or sequential logic incorrect

descriptors.full: const/let used; functions are well-named; output is clear and labelled; main() orchestrates the flow; no var
descriptors.partial: Minor issues — unclear output or inconsistent function naming
descriptors.none: var used, unreadable output, or code structure is confusing
